notes: Ethereum mainnet configuration. LaunchToken is the zero-argument IMD Index (IMDEX) project token; IndexVault issues separate vIMDEX vault shares. The seven application contracts are listed in constructor dependency order. TimelockedAdmin receives the policy owner through $owner and starts with a 172800-second delay. The reserve is mainnet WETH (18 decimals); native ETH fees are wrapped by FeeWaterfall. IndexVault starts with a 100 WETH NAV deposit cap. The PoolManager literal is the Ethereum mainnet Uniswap v4 deployment. No privileged wallet is hard-coded. The factory launch pool pairs IMDEX with native ETH and uses the factory-supplied initialization-only guard. Its manifest fee tier and price do not attach the project fee hook or override launch policy. FeeHookDeployer fixes the arguments for a later permission-bit-compatible FeeHook deployment using a mined salt. That hook serves a separate native ETH/IMDEX pool; it is not installed on the factory launch pool. The separate hooked pool starts with a 1% project fee and the 40/25/20/10/5 waterfall; fee parameters are timelocked, with LP fees accruing in the pool. Basket fees accumulate as WETH and fund vault shares owned by TimelockedAdmin. No initialization calls are included. Constructors leave guardian, signers, quorum, keeper and authorized executor unset; deposits and trading are initially disabled. Later timelocked governance must configure separate roles, feeds, token/router allowlists, methodology and bucket recipients. The hook also requires subsequent deployment, pool initialization and liquidity. EpochManager checks signed proposals for at most five assets; defaults include a six-hour proposal delay and weekly activation. RebalanceExecutor enforces delta limits, a reserve buffer and oracle output floors. Repeated trade failures block further buys without changing targets, bypassing execution windows or vetoing signed proposals; confirmed quarantine is separate. In-kind redemptions remain available without a keeper after the deposit-block share lock. Strict redemption reverts on a failed asset balance read or transfer; non-strict redemption skips it, emits RedemptionSkipped and forfeits that slice. Daily research, ranking evidence and security assessments are off-chain inputs; this manifest does not deliver a swarm service or a CoW settlement adapter. Mainnet-fork validation, independent audit and operational readiness remain prerequisites to real funds. These notes describe the accepted implementation and do not authorize deployment actions.
